context: V1 — profiled for diffing against NFTMinterV2 only. Not the primary audit focus.
purpose: V1 ERC1155 claim-NFT minter. Same pay-and-mint flow as V2 but the caller supplies the `token` argument (validated against dispatcher.primeToken()). Tracks token->indexes mapping (getDispatchers). No mintFor / authorizedMinters / replaceDispatcher.

verifiedProperties.pauseMechanism: custom `paused` bool gating mint; pause/unpause by pauser

diffVsV2: mint() takes an explicit `token` arg and require(dispatcherToken == token); V2 removes the arg and reads primeToken() directly (H-01 fix — V1 still safe via the equality check but exposes the arg).
V1 has _tokenToIndexes + getDispatchers(token); V2 drops them.
V1 lacks mintFor/authorizedMinters, replaceDispatcher, and the dispatch hook/reentrancy-guard machinery.
V1 dispatcher base (ATokenDispatcher) has NO ReentrancyGuard; V2 added it.
registerDispatcher in V1 reads primeToken() at registration; V2 reads it per-mint.

localFindings.description: Same post-dispatch _mint receiver-callback reentrancy surface as V2, but V1 dispatchers are NOT nonReentrant. Out of primary scope (V1 is context); noted for completeness in case V1 remains deployed alongside V2.
localFindings.recommendation: If V1 stays live, treat its dispatch path as reentrancy-unguarded in interaction analysis.

externalEntryPoints.function: mint(address token, uint256 index, address recipient[, bytes])

stateVariables.name: configs/dispatcherToIndex/tokenIdToDispatcher/authorizedBurners/pauser/paused/nextIndex
mutators: owner setters + price bump in mint

valueFlows: Same pay->dispatcher->mint flow as V2; payment token explicitly passed and equality-checked.
trustAssumptions: Owner registers honest dispatchers; pauser trusted; standard ERC20 prime tokens.
